title: WerbEquipmentProfile
description: Profile of a brewing setup (HLT, mash tun, kettle, fermenter) used to compute volumes, losses, and efficiency for a brew session.

name.description: Human-readable name of the equipment profile (e.g. 'Brewzilla 35L', 'Cooler MLT + propane kettle').

batch_size_l.description: Target finished batch volume into the fermenter, in liters.

efficiency_pct.description: Total brewhouse efficiency, percent (mash + lauter + boil losses considered).

hlt.description: Hot liquor tank — vessel where strike and sparge water are heated.

grain_absorption_l_per_kg.description: Liters of water absorbed per kg of grain. Typical: 0.8-1.0 L/kg.

mash_thickness_l_per_kg.description: Strike-water-to-grain ratio for the mash, in L/kg. The recipe's first mash-step infusion still wins when present; this is the brewer's default for recipes that don't carry their own mash schedule. Typical range: 2.5–4 L/kg.

evaporation_rate_l_per_hour.description: Boil-off rate in L/hour. Typical: 2-4 L/h depending on kettle and burner.

post_boil_shrinkage_pct.description: Volume reduction percentage from boiling temperature to room temperature.

post_boil_shrinkage_l.description: Post-boil hot→cold contraction as an absolute volume (L) instead of a percentage. When set, it overrides post_boil_shrinkage_pct — for brewers who'd rather enter a measured number of liters than a percentage.

trub_loss_l.description: Volume left behind as trub/yeast cake when transferring to packaging.

chilling.description: How the wort is cooled after flameout. Hops keep adding bitterness while the wort is above ~80 °C, so this feeds the IBU estimate.

method.description: 'chiller' = forced cooling (immersion, counterflow, plate, ice bath). 'no_chill' = the wort cools on its own (covered kettle or cube).

minutes_to_80c.description: Measured minutes from flameout until the wort is below 80 °C. When omitted: 0 for 'chiller' (instant), 60 for 'no_chill'. Typical: chiller 0-5, no-chill pot 30-60, no-chill cube 90-150.

transfer_loss_l.description: Volume lost during transfers between vessels (kettle to fermenter, fermenter to package).

mash_mode.description: How this rig mashes. 'classic' = mash tun + separate sparge. 'biab' = brew in a bag, all water in the kettle, lift the bag, no sparge. 'single_vessel' = all-in-one (Brewzilla / Grainfather): mash and boil in one vessel but still sparge — water math is the classic mash+sparge split, just without a separate HLT or mash tun.

sparge_method.description: How this rig sparges. 'fly' = continuous: water trickles onto the bed at ~75 °C. 'batch' = drain, add a run of water, stir, drain: the water has to be hotter to bring the bed to ~75 °C, and a small mash tun splits it into several runs. Ignored for 'biab'.
